steps.say: Transposition builds two separate circulations that never meet. The aorta arises from the right ventricle while the pulmonary artery arises from the left, so blue blood loops around the body and pink blood loops around the lungs. Without a bridge between the loops, the baby cannot survive without mixing.
steps.tx: **D-TGA** features **ventriculoarterial discordance**: the **aorta arises from the right ventricle** and the **pulmonary artery from the left ventricle**, creating two **parallel circulations** that run independently. Systemic venous blood recirculates to the body and pulmonary venous blood recirculates to the lungs. Survival demands an **obligatory mixing site**: a **patent ductus arteriosus**, **atrial septal defect**, or **ventricular septal defect**.

steps.say: The transposed newborn looks alarming from the first minutes. Profound central cyanosis resists oxygen, the chest works hard, and pulses stay full because the pump itself is strong. Bedside examination finds a deeply blue but vigorous baby, which is itself a clue toward transposition.
steps.tx: The transposed neonate shows profound **central cyanosis** unresponsive to oxygen with a single loud S2 and often no murmur. Precordial activity feels vigorous because both ventricles pump against full loads. Careful **bedside cardiovascular examination** of colour, pulses, and precordial impulses separates transposition from pulmonary disease before the echo confirms it.

steps.say: The chest film in transposition has its own classic shape. The great vessels line up anteroposteriorly instead of side by side, and the thymus involutes, so the upper mediastinum narrows into the egg on a string silhouette. Lung markings look heavy because pulmonary flow is increased.
steps.tx: The classic **egg-on-a-string appearance** shows a narrow **superior mediastinal shadow** from **anteroposterior great vessel alignment** plus **thymic involution**, with an ovoid cardiac shadow below. Increased **pulmonary vascular markings** reflect high lung flow from the left ventricle. The combination of a narrow pedicle with plethora points toward transposition rather than Fallot.

steps.say: While the surgeons prepare, the atrial septum can be opened at the bedside. The Rashkind balloon septostomy tears the septum under echocardiographic guidance, creating a large unrestrictive interatrial communication. Mixing jumps at once, saturations climb, and acidosis eases.
steps.tx: **Balloon atrial septostomy (Rashkind septostomy)** is performed percutaneously or at the **bedside under echocardiographic guidance** to create a large **unrestrictive interatrial communication**. Improved mixing raises systemic saturation within minutes and stabilises acidosis. Prostaglandin infusion keeps the ductus open alongside it until definitive repair.

Inflated pull tears a wide atrial opening

steps.say: The arterial switch restores normal plumbing. The Jatene operation transects both great vessels, switches them back to the correct ventricles, reimplanting the coronary arteries into the new aorta. Done in time, it gives an anatomical correction with the left ventricle driving the body.
steps.tx: The **arterial switch operation (Jatene procedure)** is the definitive **anatomical correction**: both great vessels are transected and switched with **coronary artery reimplantation** into the neo aorta. The left ventricle resumes systemic duty with its own valve and coronaries. Coronary transfer is the delicate step, and its anatomy decides surgical risk more than any other factor.

steps.say: Timing is everything because the left ventricle forgets quickly. With an intact ventricular septum the left ventricle pumps only to the low resistance lungs, so its muscle mass regresses within days. The switch must happen in the first 2 to 3 weeks of life, before the ventricle can no longer face body pressures.
steps.tx: For **arterial switch** the **Jatene procedure window** is the **first 2-3 weeks** of life when the **ventricular septum is intact**, before **left ventricular mass regresses**. A ventricle trained only on low pulmonary resistance fails suddenly against systemic afterload. A large VSD or ductus that keeps left sided pressures up extends the window and changes the plan.

steps.say: A different transposition often hides into adult life, surfacing decades later. Congenitally corrected transposition combines atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, leaving the morphologic right ventricle as the systemic pump. Many patients reach adulthood before the struggling systemic right ventricle declares failure.
steps.tx: **Congenitally corrected transposition (L-TGA)** carries both **atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance**, so the **morphologic right ventricle** becomes the **systemic ventricle**. Blood flows correctly despite double discordance, which is why the lesion hides for years. Systemic tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction surface in adolescence or adult life.

steps.say: The corrected form carries an electrical curse. Its conduction bundle runs an elongated abnormal course that fibroses with time, so spontaneous complete atrioventricular block strikes at about 2 percent per year for life. Every patient needs lifelong rhythm surveillance and a low threshold for pacing.
steps.tx: **Heart block in L-TGA** develops as **spontaneous complete atrioventricular block** at approximately **2 percent per year** throughout life from an elongated **abnormal conduction bundle**. Risk never plateaus, so annual ECG and Holter review continues indefinitely. Progressive PR lengthening, bundle branch block, or symptoms earn an **electrophysiology review** and usually a pacemaker before syncope strikes.
